title: Introduction to oasr
text: oasr package provides comprehensive toolkit option-adjusted spread (OAS) analysis fixed income securities, focus asset-backed securities (ABS) mortgage-backed securities (MBS). vignette demonstrates basic workflow performing OAS analysis using package.

title: Introduction to oasr
text: First, need simulate interest rate paths using dnsr package’s DNS model capabilities: Let’s visualize simulated rate paths:  look yield curves different time points:
code: # In a real analysis, we would calibrate DNS parameters from market data # dns_params <- dnsr::get_calibrated_dns_params()  # For this vignette, we'll create some sample parameters dns_params <- list(   params = list(     kappa = c(0.02, 0.3, 0.5),     # Mean-reversion speeds     theta = c(0.04, -0.02, 0.01),  # Long-run means     sigma = c(0.005, 0.01, 0.02),  # Volatilities     names = c("Level", "Slope", "Curvature"),     lambda = 0.7308   ),   initial_factors = c(0.035, -0.015, 0.005),   # The decay rate is per year, as `maturities` below is. Diebold and   # Li's conventional 0.0609 is per month, hence 0.0609 * 12 here.   lambda = 0.7308 )  # Simulate 100 interest rate paths for 360 months (30 years) # engine = "exact" samples the exact transition law, so the vignette builds # without the optional yuima package. rate_paths <- simulate_rates(dns_params, n_paths = 10, n_periods = 360, seed = 42,                              maturities = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 30),                              engine = "exact") # Plot 10 random paths of the 10-year rate plot_rate_paths(rate_paths, maturity = "10", sample_size = 10) # Plot yield curves at different time points plot_yield_curves(rate_paths, time_points = c(0, 1, 5, 10, 20), path_idx = 1)

title: Introduction to oasr
text: Next, need define prepayment model specifies loans prepay response various factors:
code: # Create a CPR/CDR prepayment model prepay_model <- prepayment_model(   type = "cpr_cdr",   base_cpr = 0.06,         # 6% CPR base rate   base_cdr = 0.01,         # 1% CDR base rate   recovery_rate = 0.65,    # 65% recovery on defaults   recovery_lag = 12,       # 12-month lag to recovery   seasoning = 1.0,         # Seasoning multiplier   burnout_factor = 0.3,    # Burnout factor   rate_sensitivity = 1.0   # Sensitivity to rate changes )  # Alternative: Use a PSA model psa_model <- psa_prepayment_model(   psa_multiplier = 1.0,    # 100% PSA   base_cdr = 0.01,         # 1% CDR base rate   recovery_rate = 0.65     # 65% recovery on defaults )  # Alternative: Use a survival model survival_model <- survival_prepayment_model(   prepay_hazard = 0.005,   # 0.5% monthly prepayment hazard   default_hazard = 0.001,  # 0.1% monthly default hazard   recovery_rate = 0.65     # 65% recovery on defaults )

text: comprehensive toolkit option-adjusted spread (OAS) analysis fixed income securities embedded options. Provides functions modeling prepayments, defaults, interest rates calculate accurate option-adjusted spreads. Supports various prepayment default models, including CPR (Conditional Prepayment Rate), CDR (Conditional Default Rate), time--event survival models.
